gen_risks.description: Extreme geographic insularity and isolation of Príncipe island (>170 km from São Tomé) could delay technical center construction and restrict logistics and service delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish early logistics planning, prioritize local material sourcing, and maintain strong operational coordination with the Regional Government of Príncipe.
gen_risks.evidence: The other main island, Príncipe—home to just about 10,000 people—is more than 170 km away and experiences compounded isolation.

gen_risks.description: Frequent climate hazards such as flooding, severe storms, and sea level rise may disrupt project training schedules, damage facilities, and affect beneficiary livelihoods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply climate-resilient design standards (including EDGE certification) for training infrastructure and embed climate adaptation practices into training curricula.
gen_risks.evidence: Key climate and disaster risks that may affect the project include floods, droughts, and rising sea levels.

gen_risks.description: Unreliable power grid infrastructure and extreme weather events could disrupt the operation of the new labor market information system and digital Employability Portal.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure backup power generators for systems infrastructure, adopt cloud-based data architecture, and enable offline-capable data entry solutions.
gen_risks.evidence: specifically intense rainfall and floods which may disrupt electricity access, the project will support the purchase of power generators

gen_risks.description: Friction and coordination delays across multiple institutional stakeholders (MLSSS, MECSHE, MEYST, MAFRD, MEF, AFAP) could cause administrative bottlenecks and delayed workplans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a unified PIU under MLSSS and leverage a strategic Ministerial Coordination Committee to streamline inter-agency approvals and oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in preparing annual workplans and implementing interventions due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders;

gen_risks.description: Delays in recording financial transactions, generating reports, or completing timely internal audits at AFAP could undermine financial controls and trigger disbursement delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a dedicated project accountant, customize the computerized accounting system, update the FM manual, and expand external auditor scope within six months.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in recording financial transactions... internal audit reviews not conducted in a timely manner, leading to identification of weak controls

gen_risks.description: Non-compliance with established eligibility criteria during beneficiary selection could cause delays or misallocations in availing sub-grants, stipends, and inclusion scholarships.
gen_risks.mitigation: Leverage objective Unique Social Registry (USR) data for targeting, detail clear eligibility criteria in the POM, and contract a professional Payment Service Provider.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in availing funds for beneficiaries resulting from possible non-compliance in selection criteria.

gen_risks.description: Delays by MLSSS/DTEFP in supplying technical inputs, Terms of Reference, and specifications to AFAP could stall procurement processes for civil works, equipment, and consultancies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit specialized technical consultants (TVET specialist, IT assistant) into the unified PIU early and set service-level agreements for procurement inputs in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: as the Ministry will need to provide technical inputs, including Terms of Reference and technical specifications, to allow AFAP to initiate procurement

gen_risks.description: Social exclusion of disadvantaged youth, low-income women, or remote residents and potential elite capture could undermine equitable distribution of grants and scholarships.
gen_risks.mitigation: Target at least 50% of beneficiaries from the USR, enforce 50% female participation quotas, and conduct inclusive community outreach via local women's associations.
gen_risks.evidence: risks of exclusion, which may arise if project benefits are not equitably distributed... as well as risks of elite capture

gen_risks.description: Young female beneficiaries face potential sexual exploitation, abuse, and sexual harassment (SEA/SH) risks during training cohorts, internship placements, and work environments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a dedicated Social/GBV Specialist, enforce binding codes of conduct across partner institutions and employers, and implement a confidential Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: community health and safety risks, including risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH), particularly for young women

gen_risks.description: Minor rehabilitation, new construction, and sub-grant-funded micro-enterprise activities could cause localized pollution, waste accumulation, or pressure on sensitive island ecosystems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint an Environmental Specialist with occupational health and safety expertise, enforce ESF screening for business sub-grants, and adopt strict construction waste protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: activities may result in the generation of solid waste... grants could support micro-enterprises in agriculture, fisheries, or tourism that may indirectly place pressure on sensitive ecosystems

gen_risks.description: Limited domestic private sector absorption capacity in STP's small economy may impede trained youth from securing sustained wage employment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Combine skills training with self-employment starter packages, MSME booster grants, and structured labor mobility pathways to expand job opportunities abroad.
gen_risks.evidence: Micro and small enterprises make up 92 percent of all firms... mostly household-run and provide few job opportunities... limited absorption capacity of the domestic labor market

gen_risks.description: High youth desire for emigration (68%) combined with unstructured migration channels could result in brain drain, worker exploitation abroad, and reduced project retention.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate safe, market-aligned labor mobility orientation modules, partner with key destination countries (e.g., Portugal), and link Employability Portal with overseas job options.
gen_risks.evidence: 68 percent of youth are considering leaving... emigration has yielded limited economic benefits... migrants end up in precarious jobs with low wages

gen_risks.description: Failure to recruit key legal covenant specialists (Environmental, Social/GBV, TVET, IT) within 45 to 60 days post-effectiveness could delay project startup.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate TOR drafting and recruitment preparation during the pre-effectiveness window to ensure rapid appointment post-effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: hire or appoint, not later than forty-five (45) days after Effectiveness: (i) one Environmental Specialist... (ii) one Social Specialist...

gen_risks.description: Construction cost overruns and material price inflation for the new technical training center in Príncipe could exceed the preliminary $5 million budget allocation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Complete detailed engineering designs and local cost studies early, and manage potential budget adjustments dynamically within the project procurement plan.
gen_risks.evidence: The cost estimate for the new center is based on preliminary technical inputs... Adjustments will be managed within project's procurement plan

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
